note: Two rulings about WHERE a type relation is anchored, both found as symmetric misses/fabrications where the COUNTS matched exactly and every key was wrong - the most misleading failure a completeness gate can have. CLJ-D48: the source is the analyzer's `activeFunction`, which is set by FUNCTION FORMS and not by `def`. A `reify` attributes to the enclosing definition (core.clj:7291 publishes `future-call -> clojure.lang.IDeref`), while a `proxy` inside a `def` INITIALISER has no enclosing function and falls back to the NAMESPACE (instant.clj:162 publishes `clojure.instant -> ThreadLocal`, not the var it builds). The existing comment asserted the opposite and was half right: written about `proxy`, applied to `reify`. I first 'corrected' the proxy superclass on the strength of ONE sample and made `extends` worse - 7 wrong of 39 becoming 33 - which is why the rule here is stated as a measurement rather than a generalisation. CLJ-D49: a namespace's aliases survive two shapes that were unread. The `ns` form carries METADATA between head and name, so the name came back as `^{:no-doc true} clj.fixture.typerel`; and the `:require` mixes a PREFIX LIST with a plain spec, and a prefix list was detected by asking whether its first child was a symbol - which a prefix list ALSO has, so `[protocols :as p]` was silently skipped. The measured symptom was an alias table of size 1 where two aliases existed. Pins all four positions.
